A1.justification: Both 15-page PDFs describe the same VAOT/VASOT research. The text, equations, eight tables, nine figures and Appendices A.1–A.7 support reliable comparison despite pagination shifts.

before.justification: v2 reports original VAOT/VASOT benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity analyses, qualitative evaluations and computational measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original VAOT/VASOT benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity analyses, qualitative evaluations and computational measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same VAOT balanced FGW procedure and VASOT joint objective, including structural and temporal priors, virtual-frame handling, encoders and learning losses.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate alignment on Pouring, Penn Action and IKEA ASM, and segmentation on Breakfast, YouTube Instructions, 50 Salads and Desktop Assembly. Appendix evaluation coverage is also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership and participation are identical in Tables 2, 3, 7 and 8, including the TWF, ABD and ASOT baselines in the appendix per-video comparison.

E3.justification: The splits, encoders, metrics and hyperparameters remain unchanged. Both versions retain the shared-encoder Penn Action evaluation and the distinction between dataset-level and per-video Hungarian matching in Appendices A.4–A.5.

E4.justification: The component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, retrieval and segmentation examples, t-SNE analysis and Appendix A.7 complexity comparison are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and sensitivity curves. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–3 and 6–8, plotted findings and Appendix A.7 measurements match. For example, VAOT's Pouring Acc@1.0 remains 94.63 in Table 2, and its multi-action Penn Action Progress remains 79.23 in Table 7.

T1.justification: The optimal-transport definitions, constraints, objectives and losses in Equations 1–7 are unchanged, as are the solver derivation and complexity reasoning. No formal results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same methodological, novelty, performance and efficiency claims. The added code-access statement does not revise the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations for balanced alignment, the asymmetric benefits of joint learning, and the qualitative and complexity interpretations remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit statement in the abstract that code is available through the authors' research website, with a corresponding hyperlink. v2 provides only the company homepage. Implementation details, hyperparameters and hardware information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 84 works and retain the same research positioning. Changes to bibliography page back-references reflect pagination rather than changed citations.

P1.justification: A code-access sentence is appended to the abstract, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Scientific prose, terminology and section order are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figures and table designs remain unchanged, but text reflow moves Table 8 from PDF page 10 to 11, the conclusion's ending onto page 9, and the references' start from page 11 to 12.

improvement.justification: The new explicit code-access statement and research-site link modestly improve reproducibility guidance by giving readers a clearer route to the implementation. Scientific content and evidence are unchanged; the supplied PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
